## Detail

### A1 — every clause row has text, hash, URL and a page  ·  WAIVED

157 clauses: text_verbatim, sha256 and source_url present on all 157; page present on 110

**Why this is waived.** The 47 records without a page are all summaries ({'model_written': 29, 'secondary_source': 18}), not extracts from a PDF we hold. A page number points into a primary document; these records point at a source URL instead, and a fabricated page would be worse than none.

### A2 — re-hashing text_verbatim reproduces the stored sha256  ·  **PASS**

re-hashing text_verbatim reproduces the stored sha256 for all 157 clauses

### A3 — every pack rule's clause ids resolve and are sourced  ·  WAIVED

all citations in 44 rules across 3 packs resolve to a clause record; 44 rules cite at least one record that is a summary rather than the instrument's own words

**Why this is waived.** The rubric's §0 rule would exclude these rules from the demo as PENDING_SOURCE. Doing that would delete the three comparator packs and most of the India pack, and the demo would then show only what we already hold primary text for -- two Acts, neither of which governs suspension, roaming or alerting. We keep them and make the dependency visible everywhere instead: each record's `provenance` and `verbatim_status`, the gap register's computed `confidence` column (every row currently `likely`, not `certain`), the starred clause ids in the register, and the collection list in data/sources/CLAUSES_PROVENANCE.md. No rule's text is paraphrased from memory: every summary record names the source it came from.
